scope: Proposition 3.3 (Boundary line) of the manuscript “Projective Hodge lines and ordinary Iitaka subadditivity” (preprints/Projective-Hodge-lines-and-ordinary-Iitaka-subadditivity-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 564a98c625b94ef4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On a transverse coordinate chart (u, v) about a general point of E, with E = (u = 0), write a generator of the lifted Hodge line as (3.2) ezN a(u, v), z = log u 2πi , where a is holomorphic across u = 0 and a(0, v) ̸= 0. After shrinking the chart there is an integer ℓ ≥ 0 such that (3.3) Nℓ+1 a(0, v) = 0, Nℓ a(0, v) ̸= 0, and the line belongs to weight w + ℓ in the limiting mixed Hodge structure. Moreover, (3.4) ν(J|E) ≤ rkgen d v 7−→ [Nℓ a(0, v)]  . The map on the right is formed in the chosen flat coordinates. If N = 0, take ℓ = 0; the variation then extends purely near the general point of E.
